title: Combining Directional Invariant Information in LS-Design Attacks
summary: Each LS-design direction generically preserves only its own class of structure; it remains open whether their partial invariant information can be combined into an attack.

formal_statement.body: For an LS-design built from an S-box direction and an L-box direction, determine whether there exists a cryptanalytic attack that combines partial invariant information from both directions when neither layer, considered generically on its own, preserves the full invariant property. The relevant direction-specific results establish generic preservation of equality spaces in one direction and of linear spaces or cosets in the other; the unresolved task is to exploit a combination of these partial preservation properties to obtain an attack despite the absence of a fully generic invariant in either direction.

scope.domain: Structural cryptanalysis of LS-designs using invariant information from their S-box and L-box directions.
assumptions: Neither direction, considered generically on its own, preserves the full invariant property.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether an attack can combine partial invariant information from the S-box and L-box directions despite neither direction alone preserving a fully generic invariant.

citations.label: A Generic Approach to Invariant Subspace Attacks: Cryptanalysis of Robin, iSCREAM and Zorro

progress.summary: The paper establishes the generic structures preserved in each direction and presents attacks realizing those direction-specific properties. It explicitly leaves open whether partial information from both directions can be combined when neither supplies a fully generic invariant.
citation_labels: Gregor Leander et al., A Generic Approach to Invariant Subspace Attacks: Cryptanalysis of Robin, iSCREAM and Zorro
